hero.title: Founding Engineer & SEO Expert at Welup Digital
hero.overview: First developer hire. Co-built the original platform, then rewrote it all in Next.js when the business needed something faster and easier to update. Also set up the CMS, handled technical SEO, and taught web development at their academy.

challenge.problem: The old site was built in pure JS. My endpoint kept getting DDoSed because of how I set it up back then. No CMS, terrible for SEO, and the CSS was a mess - so many classes that it slowed everything down as the site grew.
constraints: Migrating from a legacy static site
Solo developer doing the rewrite and CMS
Had to keep the site running during the migration
challenge.context: Welup was growing fast and needed a site that could handle more content, rank on Google, and actually survive a DDoS attack.
metrics: Static site: no CMS, poor SEO
No blog or landing page system

primary: Rewrite in Next.js for better performance and SEO
Set up a CMS so non-devs could update content
Get proper hosting that doesn't go down
stakeholder: Keep the site live during the switch

approach.methodology: Did it piece by piece. Migrated one section at a time, kept SEO and performance in mind the whole way through.

phases.name: CMS & Content
activities: Built blog and landing page templates

phases.name: Security & Uptime
activities: Kept the site up through attacks

phases.name: SEO & Academy
activities: Taught web dev and SEO at Welup Academy

keyDecisions.decision: Moved to Next.js and server components
keyDecisions.rationale: Faster, better for SEO, easier to maintain
Flexible content management without the headache

research: Looked at what top agencies were doing
Listened to user feedback on speed and navigation
approach.collaboration: First hire. Built the first version with someone else, then took over the rewrite and everything else tech.
iterations: Improved the CMS based on what people actually used
approach.userFeedback: The founders and academy students said the new site is faster and easier to use. SEO started actually working.

metrics: CMS for blogs and landing pages

testimonials.name: Adaeze Nwosu
testimonials.quote: Andy is leading our web platform’s transformation—our new CMS and site are fast, reliable, and easy for the whole team. Our SEO and client delivery have never been stronger.

achievements: Major SEO and client delivery wins
Built foundational CMS and content systems

hero.title: SEO & Growth Specialist at PromptEarn
hero.overview: Spent 6 months there doing SEO and affiliate growth. Got their organic traffic up 250% and hit top 5 rankings for key terms. Fixed the slow page speeds, expanded the affiliate network, and set up proper tracking.

challenge.problem: PromptEarn needed more traffic and affiliate sales. The site was slow, Google wasn't ranking it, and the affiliate program was stuck.
constraints: Big affiliate base that needed managing
Needed results they could actually measure
challenge.context: Affiliate marketing and SEO are brutal in the Nigerian fintech space. PromptEarn wanted to beat the competition by getting the technical stuff right and growing their affiliate network.

primary: Land top 5 spots for target keywords
stakeholder: More sales from search and referrals
success: Showing up in search for core terms

approach.methodology: Worked in weekly sprints. Quick audits first, then tackled the bigger stuff. Measured everything along the way.

keyDecisions.decision: Focused on Core Web Vitals first
keyDecisions.rationale: Made a real dent in bounce rate
Growth happened much faster after that

research: Asked users about speed and navigation
approach.collaboration: Weekly syncs with marketing and devs, monthly check-ins with the people paying the bills.
iterations: Landing pages got better as we watched bounce rate data
approach.userFeedback: Affiliates and users both said the site felt faster and was easier to figure out.

metrics: Top 1% search visibility for niche keywords
achievements: Dominant search presence for target keywords
